speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the rash first appeared and if it started on your face or trunk before spreading? Also, have you noticed any swelling around your eyes or joints?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain, redness, or swelling in your hands, feet, or joints? Also, has the rash changed color or become purplish?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling, particularly in your hands or knees? Also, does the rash fade when you press on it, or does it remain red?

speaker: Doctor

REQUEST IMAGES

The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild systemic symptoms, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
